title: Two Sum
description:
Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to target.

You may assume each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice.

Input: line 1 is the array, e.g. [2,7,11,15]; line 2 is the target.
Output: the two indices, e.g. [0,1].

examples.explanation: nums[0] + nums[1] == 9.

title: Valid Parentheses
description:
Given a string s containing just the characters '()[]{}', determine if the input string is valid.

An input string is valid if open brackets are closed by the same type of bracket and in the correct order.

Output: 'true' or 'false'.

title: Reverse String
description: Write a function that reverses a string. The input is a single line of text. Output the reversed string.

title: Maximum Subarray
description:
Given an integer array nums, find the contiguous subarray (containing at least one number) with the largest sum and return that sum.

Input: a single line containing the array, e.g. [-2,1,-3].
Output: the maximum subarray sum as a single integer.

examples.explanation: The subarray [4,-1,2,1] has the largest sum 6.
The whole array sums to 23.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description:
Given a string s, return the length of the longest substring that contains no repeating characters.

Input: a single line containing the string s (it may be empty). The test strings contain no spaces.
Output: the length as a single integer.

examples.explanation: The answer is "abc", with length 3.
The answer is "b", with length 1.
The answer is "wke". Note "pwke" is a subsequence, not a substring.

constraints: s consists of English letters, digits and symbols (no spaces in tests).

title: House Robber
description:
You are a robber planning to rob houses along a street. Each house has some money, but adjacent houses have connected security systems that trigger if two adjacent houses are robbed on the same night.

Given an integer array nums representing the money in each house, return the maximum amount you can rob without alerting the police.

Input: a single line containing the array, e.g. [2,7,9,3,1].
Output: the maximum amount as a single integer.

examples.explanation: Rob house 0 (1) and house 2 (3): total 4.
Rob houses 0, 2 and 4: 2 + 9 + 1 = 12.

title: Coin Change
description:
You are given coins of different denominations and a total amount of money. Return the fewest number of coins needed to make up that amount. If it cannot be made from any combination of the coins, return -1. You have an unlimited number of each coin.

Input: line 1 is the coins array, e.g. [1,2,5]; line 2 is the target amount.
Output: the fewest number of coins (or -1) as a single integer.

examples.explanation: 3 cannot be made from only 2s.

title: Number of Islands
description:
Given a 2D grid of "1" (land) and "0" (water), count the number of islands. An island is surrounded by water and is formed by connecting adjacent lands horizontally or vertically (not diagonally).

Input: a single line containing the grid as a list of row strings, e.g. ["11110","11010"].
Output: the number of islands as a single integer.

examples.explanation: All the land cells are connected into one island.
Three separate land groups.

title: Trapping Rain Water
description:
Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.

Input: a single line containing the heights array, e.g. [0,1,0,2,1,0,1,3,2,1,2,1].
Output: the total units of trapped water as a single integer.

examples.explanation: The elevation map traps 6 units of water.

title: Edit Distance
description:
Given two strings word1 and word2, return the minimum number of operations required to convert word1 into word2. The permitted operations are: insert a character, delete a character, or replace a character.

Input: line 1 is word1; line 2 is word2.
Output: the minimum number of operations as a single integer.

examples.explanation: horse -> rorse (replace h) -> rose (delete r) -> ros (delete e).

constraints: Both strings consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Contains Duplicate
description:
Given an integer array nums, return true if any value appears at least twice, and false if every element is distinct.

Input: a single line containing the array, e.g. [1,2,3,1].
Output: 'true' or 'false'.

title: Valid Anagram
description:
Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s, and false otherwise. An anagram uses all the original letters exactly once.

Input: line 1 is s; line 2 is t.
Output: 'true' or 'false'.
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
description:
You are given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a stock on day i. You want to maximise profit by choosing a single day to buy and a later day to sell.

Return the maximum profit you can achieve. If no profit is possible, return 0.

Input: a single line containing the prices array, e.g. [7,1,5,3,6,4].
Output: the maximum profit as a single integer.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 1 (price 1) and sell on day 4 (price 6): profit 5.
Prices only fall, so no profit is possible.

title: Climbing Stairs
description:
You are climbing a staircase that takes n steps to reach the top. Each time you can climb either 1 or 2 steps. In how many distinct ways can you reach the top?

Input: a single line containing the integer n.
Output: the number of distinct ways as a single integer.

title: Binary Search
description:
Given a sorted (ascending) array of distinct integers nums and a target, return the index of target if it is present, otherwise return -1. Your algorithm should run in O(log n) time.

Input: line 1 is the array, e.g. [-1,0,3,5,9,12]; line 2 is the target.
Output: the index (or -1) as a single integer.
constraints: nums is sorted in ascending order and all values are distinct.

title: Majority Element
description:
Given an array nums of size n, return the majority element - the element that appears more than n/2 times (rounded down). You may assume the majority element always exists.

Input: a single line containing the array, e.g. [2,2,1,1,1,2,2].
Output: the majority element as a single integer.
constraints: A majority element always exists in the array.

title: Single Number
description:
Given a non-empty array nums where every element appears exactly twice except for one, find that single element. Aim for linear time and constant extra space.

Input: a single line containing the array, e.g. [4,1,2,1,2].
Output: the element that appears once, as a single integer.
constraints: Every element appears twice except for one which appears once.

title: Product of Array Except Self
description:
Given an integer array nums, return an array answer such that answer[i] equals the product of all elements of nums except nums[i]. Solve it without using the division operator.

Input: a single line containing the array, e.g. [1,2,3,4].
Output: the answer array, e.g. [24,12,8,6].
constraints: The product of any prefix or suffix fits in a 32-bit integer.

title: Move Zeroes
description:
Given an integer array nums, move all 0s to the end while keeping the relative order of the non-zero elements. Return the resulting array.

Input: a single line containing the array, e.g. [0,1,0,3,12].
Output: the resulting array, e.g. [1,3,12,0,0].

title: Longest Common Prefix
description:
Write a function to find the longest common prefix string amongst an array of strings. If there is no common prefix, return an empty string.

Input: a single line containing the strings, e.g. ["flower","flow","flight"].
Output: the longest common prefix (an empty line if there is none).

examples.explanation: There is no common prefix.

constraints: strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Roman to Integer
description:
Given a Roman numeral, convert it to an integer. Roman numerals use the symbols I, V, X, L, C, D and M. When a smaller numeral precedes a larger one it is subtracted (e.g. IV = 4, IX = 9, XL = 40).

Input: a single line containing the Roman numeral.
Output: the integer value.
constraints: s is a valid Roman numeral in the range [1, 3999].

title: Fizz Buzz
description:
Given an integer n, return a string array answer (1-indexed) where for each i from 1 to n: answer[i] is "FizzBuzz" if i is divisible by both 3 and 5, "Fizz" if divisible by 3, "Buzz" if divisible by 5, otherwise the decimal of i as a string.

Input: a single line containing the integer n.
Output: the answer as a list of strings, e.g. ["1","2","Fizz"].

title: Vowel Count
description:
Count how many vowels (a, e, i, o, u) appear in a string. Treat the input as case-insensitive, so both 'A' and 'a' count.

Input: a single line of text (it may be empty).
Output: the number of vowels as a single integer.

examples.explanation: 'e' and 'o'.

constraints: s consists of English letters (no spaces in tests).

title: Caesar Cipher
description:
Encrypt a message with a Caesar cipher: shift each lowercase letter forward in the alphabet by a given amount, wrapping from z back to a. The shift may be larger than 26.

Input: line 1 is the message (lowercase letters only); line 2 is the integer shift.
Output: the encrypted message.

examples.explanation: z wraps around to c.

constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Run-Length Encoding
description:
Compress a string by replacing each run of consecutive identical characters with the character followed by the run length. For example "aaabbc" becomes "a3b2c1". The empty string encodes to the empty string.

Input: a single line of text (lowercase letters, possibly empty).
Output: the run-length encoded string.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Digital Root
description:
Repeatedly sum the digits of a non-negative integer until a single digit remains, and return that digit. For example 38 -> 3 + 8 = 11 -> 1 + 1 = 2.

Input: a single line containing the integer n.
Output: the digital root as a single integer.

title: Missing Number
description:
Given an array nums containing n distinct numbers taken from the range [0, n], return the one number in that range that is missing.

Input: a single line containing the array, e.g. [3,0,1].
Output: the missing number as a single integer.

examples.explanation: n = 3, so the range is [0,3]. 2 is missing.

constraints: All the numbers of nums are distinct.

title: Count Primes
description:
Given an integer n, return the number of prime numbers that are strictly less than n.

Input: a single line containing the integer n.
Output: the count of primes below n as a single integer.

examples.explanation: The primes below 10 are 2, 3, 5 and 7.

title: Reverse Integer
description:
Given a signed 32-bit integer x, return x with its digits reversed. If reversing x causes the value to fall outside the signed 32-bit integer range [-2^31, 2^31 - 1], return 0 instead.

Input: a single line containing the integer x.
Output: the reversed integer (or 0 on overflow).

examples.explanation: Trailing zeros are dropped.

title: Pangram Check
description:
A pangram is a string that contains every letter of the English alphabet at least once. Given a string s of lowercase letters, return true if it is a pangram, and false otherwise.

Input: a single line of lowercase letters (no spaces in tests).
Output: 'true' or 'false'.
constraints: s consists of lowercase English letters.

title: Container With Most Water
description:
You are given an integer array height of length n. There are n vertical lines where the i-th line has endpoints (i, 0) and (i, height[i]). Find two lines that, together with the x-axis, form a container holding the most water, and return that maximum amount.

Input: a single line containing the height array, e.g. [1,8,6,2,5,4,8,3,7].
Output: the maximum water the container can store as a single integer.

examples.explanation: Lines at index 1 and 8 (heights 8 and 7) hold 7 * 7 = 49 units.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
description:
An ascending sorted array of distinct integers is rotated at some unknown pivot (e.g. [0,1,2,4,5,6,7] might become [4,5,6,7,0,1,2]). Given the rotated array nums and an integer target, return the index of target, or -1 if it is not present. Aim for O(log n) time.

Input: line 1 is the array, e.g. [4,5,6,7,0,1,2]; line 2 is the target.
Output: the index (or -1) as a single integer.
constraints: All values of nums are distinct.
nums is an ascending array rotated at some pivot.

title: Jump Game
description:
You are given an integer array nums. You start at the first index, and each element represents your maximum jump length from that position. Return true if you can reach the last index, otherwise false.

Input: a single line containing the array, e.g. [2,3,1,1,4].
Output: 'true' or 'false'.

examples.explanation: Jump 1 step to index 1, then 3 steps to the last index.
You always land on index 3 (value 0) and cannot move further.

title: Subarray Sum Equals K
description:
Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the total number of contiguous subarrays whose elements sum to exactly k.

Input: line 1 is the array, e.g. [1,1,1]; line 2 is the integer k.
Output: the number of qualifying subarrays as a single integer.

examples.explanation: The subarrays [1,1] (indices 0-1) and [1,1] (indices 1-2).

title: Top K Frequent Elements
description:
Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements. To make the answer unique, return them ordered by frequency from highest to lowest; if two elements have the same frequency, order them by value from lowest to highest.

Input: line 1 is the array, e.g. [1,1,1,2,2,3]; line 2 is the integer k.
Output: the k elements, e.g. [1,2].

examples.explanation: 1 appears 3 times, 2 appears twice.

constraints: k is in the range [1, the number of distinct elements].

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
description:
Given an array heights representing the heights of bars in a histogram where each bar has width 1, return the area of the largest rectangle that fits entirely within the histogram.

Input: a single line containing the heights array, e.g. [2,1,5,6,2,3].
Output: the largest rectangle area as a single integer.

examples.explanation: The bars of height 5 and 6 form a 2-wide rectangle of area 10.

title: First Missing Positive
description:
Given an unsorted integer array nums, return the smallest positive integer (starting from 1) that does not appear in the array. The classic challenge is to do it in O(n) time and O(1) extra space.

Input: a single line containing the array, e.g. [3,4,-1,1].
Output: the smallest missing positive integer.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
description:
Given an integer array nums and a window size k, the window slides from the left to the right of the array one position at a time. Return an array of the maximum value within each window position.

Input: line 1 is the array, e.g. [1,3,-1,-3,5,3,6,7]; line 2 is the window size k.
Output: the array of window maxima, e.g. [3,3,5,5,6,7].

examples.explanation: Each window of 3 contributes its maximum.

title: Valid Palindrome
description:
Given a string s, return true if it is a palindrome after converting all uppercase letters to lowercase and removing all non-alphanumeric characters, and false otherwise.

Input: a single line containing the string s (it may contain spaces and punctuation).
Output: 'true' or 'false'.

examples.input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"
examples.explanation: After cleaning, "amanaplanacanalpanama" reads the same both ways.
"raceacar" is not a palindrome.

constraints: s consists of printable ASCII characters.

title: Plus One
description:
You are given a large integer represented as an integer array digits, where each digits[i] is the ith digit of the number, ordered most-significant first. Increment the integer by one and return the resulting array of digits.

The number contains no leading zeros except for the number 0 itself.

Input: a single line containing the digits array, e.g. [1,2,3].
Output: the incremented digits array, e.g. [1,2,4].

examples.explanation: The array represents 123, and 123 + 1 = 124.

constraints: digits has no leading zeros except for 0 itself.

title: Unique Paths
description:
A robot is located at the top-left corner of an m x n grid. It can only move either down or right at any point in time, and is trying to reach the bottom-right corner.

Return the number of distinct paths the robot can take.

Input: line 1 is m (the number of rows); line 2 is n (the number of columns).
Output: the number of distinct paths as a single integer.

examples.explanation: From the top-left there are 3 ways to reach the bottom-right.

constraints: The answer is guaranteed to be at most 2 * 10^9.

title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
description:
Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the kth largest element in the array. Note that it is the kth largest element in sorted order, not the kth distinct element.

Input: line 1 is the array, e.g. [3,2,1,5,6,4]; line 2 is k.
Output: the kth largest element as a single integer.

title: N-Queens (Count Solutions)
description:
The n-queens puzzle is the problem of placing n queens on an n x n chessboard so that no two queens attack each other (no two share a row, column, or diagonal).

Given an integer n, return the number of distinct solutions to the n-queens puzzle.

Input: a single line containing the integer n.
Output: the number of distinct solutions as a single integer.

examples.explanation: There are two distinct solutions to the 4-queens puzzle.

title: Regular Expression Matching
description:
Given an input string s and a pattern p, implement regular expression matching with support for '.' and '*' where:

- '.' matches any single character.
- '*' matches zero or more of the preceding element.

The match must cover the entire input string (not partial).

Input: line 1 is s; line 2 is the pattern p.
Output: 'true' or 'false'.

examples.explanation: 'a*' matches zero or more 'a', so it matches "aa".

constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters.
p contains only lowercase English letters, '.', and '*'.
It is guaranteed that for each '*' there is a previous valid character to match.

title: Reverse Linked List
description:
Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list and return the new head.

Input: a single line with the list as an array, e.g. [1,2,3,4,5]. An empty list is [].
Output: the reversed list as an array.

title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
description:
You are given the heads of two sorted singly linked lists list1 and list2. Splice them together into one sorted list and return its head.

Input: line 1 is list1, line 2 is list2, each an array, e.g. [1,2,4]. An empty list is [].
Output: the merged sorted list as an array.
constraints: 0 <= number of nodes in each list <= 50
Both lists are sorted in non-decreasing order.

title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
description:
Given the root of a binary tree, return its maximum depth: the number of nodes along the longest path from the root down to the farthest leaf.

Input: a single line with the tree in level-order (BFS) form using null for missing children, e.g. [3,9,20,null,null,15,7]. An empty tree is [].
Output: the maximum depth as a single integer.

title: Invert Binary Tree
description:
Given the root of a binary tree, invert it (swap the left and right child of every node) and return the root.

Input: a single line with the tree in level-order (BFS) form using null for missing children, e.g. [4,2,7,1,3,6,9]. An empty tree is [].
Output: the inverted tree in the same level-order array form (trailing nulls trimmed).

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
description:
Given the root of a binary tree, determine whether it is a valid binary search tree (BST). A valid BST requires every node in the left subtree to be strictly less than the node, every node in the right subtree to be strictly greater, and both subtrees to also be valid BSTs.

Input: a single line with the tree in level-order (BFS) form using null for missing children, e.g. [2,1,3]. An empty tree is [].
Output: true or false.

examples.explanation: The root's right child 4 is less than the root 5.

title: Transpose Matrix
description:
Given a 2D integer matrix, return its transpose. The transpose flips the matrix over its main diagonal, swapping rows and columns.

Input: line 1 is the matrix as a JSON array of rows, e.g. [[1,2,3],[4,5,6]].
Output: the transposed matrix, e.g. [[1,4],[2,5],[3,6]].

examples.explanation: Row i, column j of the result is row j, column i of the input.

constraints: All rows have the same length.

title: Spiral Matrix
description:
Given an m x n integer matrix, return all elements of the matrix in spiral order: start at the top-left, move right, then down, then left, then up, spiralling inward.

Input: line 1 is the matrix as a JSON array of rows, e.g. [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]].
Output: the elements in spiral order as a flat array, e.g. [1,2,3,6,9,8,7,4,5].

examples.explanation: Walk the outer ring clockwise, then the centre.

constraints: All rows have the same length.

title: Rotate Image
description:
You are given an n x n integer matrix representing an image. Rotate the image by 90 degrees clockwise and return it.

Input: line 1 is the n x n matrix as a JSON array of rows, e.g. [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]].
Output: the rotated matrix, e.g. [[7,4,1],[8,5,2],[9,6,3]].

examples.explanation: Each column read top-to-bottom becomes a row read left-to-right.

title: Set Matrix Zeroes
description:
Given an m x n integer matrix, if an element is 0, set its entire row and column to 0. Return the resulting matrix.

Input: line 1 is the matrix as a JSON array of rows, e.g. [[1,1,1],[1,0,1],[1,1,1]].
Output: the matrix after zeroing, e.g. [[1,0,1],[0,0,0],[1,0,1]].

examples.explanation: The single 0 zeroes its row and its column.

constraints: All rows have the same length.

title: Merge Intervals
description:
Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i], merge all overlapping intervals and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the intervals in the input. Intervals that only touch at an endpoint (e.g. [1,4] and [4,5]) are considered overlapping.

Input: line 1 is the intervals as a JSON array of pairs, e.g. [[1,3],[2,6],[8,10],[15,18]].
Output: the merged intervals sorted by start, e.g. [[1,6],[8,10],[15,18]].

examples.explanation: [1,3] and [2,6] overlap, so they merge into [1,6].
[1,4] and [4,5] touch at 4 and are considered overlapping.

title: Insert Interval
description:
You are given a sorted array of non-overlapping intervals (by start) and a new interval. Insert the new interval, merging with any overlapping intervals, and return the resulting sorted array of non-overlapping intervals.

Input: line 1 is the existing intervals as a JSON array of pairs, e.g. [[1,3],[6,9]]. Line 2 is the new interval as a JSON pair, e.g. [2,5].
Output: the intervals after insertion, e.g. [[1,5],[6,9]].

examples.explanation: [2,5] overlaps [1,3], merging to [1,5].

constraints: intervals is sorted by start_i and has no overlaps

title: Meeting Rooms
description:
Given an array of meeting time intervals where intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i], determine if a person could attend all meetings (i.e. no two meetings overlap). Meetings that only touch at an endpoint (e.g. [1,2] and [2,3]) do NOT conflict.

Input: line 1 is the intervals as a JSON array of pairs, e.g. [[0,30],[5,10],[15,20]].
Output: the boolean true or false.

examples.explanation: [0,30] overlaps [5,10], so not all meetings can be attended.
The two meetings do not overlap.

title: Non-overlapping Intervals
description:
Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [start_i, end_i], return the minimum number of intervals you need to remove to make the rest non-overlapping. Intervals that only touch at an endpoint (e.g. [1,2] and [2,3]) are NOT considered overlapping.

Input: line 1 is the intervals as a JSON array of pairs, e.g. [[1,2],[2,3],[3,4],[1,3]].
Output: the minimum count as an integer, e.g. 1.

examples.explanation: Remove [1,3] and the rest are non-overlapping.
Keep one [1,2] and remove the other two.

title: Power of Two
description:
Given an integer n, return true if it is a power of two, otherwise return false.

An integer is a power of two if there exists an integer x such that n == 2^x.

Input: a single line containing the integer n.
Output: 'true' or 'false'.

title: Fibonacci Number
description:
The Fibonacci numbers form a sequence where each number is the sum of the two preceding ones, starting from 0 and 1. That is, F(0) = 0, F(1) = 1, and F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2) for n > 1.

Given n, compute F(n).

Input: a single line containing the integer n.
Output: F(n) as a single integer.

title: Isomorphic Strings
description:
Given two strings s and t, determine if they are isomorphic.

Two strings are isomorphic if the characters in s can be replaced to get t. All occurrences of a character must be replaced with another character while preserving the order of characters. No two characters may map to the same character, but a character may map to itself.

Input: line 1 is s; line 2 is t.
Output: 'true' or 'false'.

examples.explanation: e -> a, g -> d.
o would need to map to both a and r.

constraints: s and t consist of any valid ASCII characters.

title: Number of 1 Bits
description:
Given a non-negative integer n, return the number of '1' bits it has in its binary representation (also known as the Hamming weight).

Input: a single integer n.
Output: the count of set bits.

examples.explanation: 1011 has three set bits.
10000000 has one set bit.
11111111 has eight set bits.

title: Max Consecutive Ones
description:
Given a binary array nums, return the maximum number of consecutive 1's in the array.

Input: a JSON array of 0s and 1s.
Output: the length of the longest run of consecutive 1's.

examples.explanation: The last three elements are all 1.
The longest run has length 2.

title: Squares of a Sorted Array
description:
Given an integer array nums sorted in non-decreasing order, return an array of the squares of each number sorted in non-decreasing order.

Input: a JSON array of integers (already sorted ascending).
Output: a JSON array of the squares, sorted ascending.

examples.explanation: Squaring gives [16,1,0,9,100], then sorted becomes [0,1,9,16,100].
Squares sorted ascending.

constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order.

title: Length of Last Word
description:
Given a string s consisting of words and spaces, return the length of the last word in the string.

A word is a maximal substring consisting of non-space characters only.

Input: a single line string s (may contain trailing spaces).
Output: the length of the last word.

examples.explanation: The last word is "World", length 5.

examples.input: s = "   fly me   to   the moon  "
examples.explanation: The last word is "moon", length 4.

constraints: s consists of only English letters and spaces ' '.
There is at least one word in s.

title: Find Pivot Index
description:
Given an array of integers nums, calculate the pivot index of this array.

The pivot index is the index where the sum of all the numbers strictly to the left of the index is equal to the sum of all the numbers strictly to the index's right.

If the index is on the left edge of the array, the left sum is 0 because there are no elements to the left. Return the leftmost pivot index. If no such index exists, return -1.

Input: a JSON array of integers.
Output: the pivot index, or -1.

examples.explanation: Left sum = 1+7+3 = 11, right sum = 5+6 = 11.
There is no index that satisfies the condition.
Left sum = 0, right sum = 1 + -1 = 0.

title: Palindrome Number
description:
Given an integer x, return true if x reads the same backward as forward.

Negative numbers are never palindromes because of the leading minus sign.

Input: a single integer.
Output: 'true' or 'false'.

examples.explanation: From left to right it reads -121; from right to left it reads 121-.

title: Hamming Distance
description:
The Hamming distance between two integers is the number of bit positions at which the corresponding bits are different.

Given two integers x and y, return their Hamming distance.

Input: line 1 is x; line 2 is y.
Output: the Hamming distance.

examples.explanation: 1 = 0001, 4 = 0100; they differ in two positions.

title: Excel Sheet Column Number
description:
Given a string columnTitle that represents the column title as it appears in an Excel sheet, return its corresponding column number.

For example: A -> 1, B -> 2, ..., Z -> 26, AA -> 27, AB -> 28, and so on.

Input: the column title (uppercase letters).
Output: the column number.
constraints: columnTitle consists only of uppercase English letters.

title: Sqrt(x)
description:
Given a non-negative integer x, return the square root of x rounded down to the nearest integer.

You must not use any built-in exponent function or operator (for example, do not use pow(x, 0.5) or x ** 0.5).

Input: a single non-negative integer.
Output: floor(sqrt(x)).

examples.explanation: sqrt(8) = 2.828..., rounded down is 2.

title: Find All Numbers Disappeared in an Array
description:
Given an array nums of n integers where nums[i] is in the range [1, n], return an array of all the integers in the range [1, n] that do not appear in nums.

Input: a JSON array of integers.
Output: a JSON array of the missing integers, in ascending order (for example [5,6]).

title: Intersection of Two Arrays
description:
Given two integer arrays nums1 and nums2, return an array of their intersection. Each element in the result must be unique.

Return the result sorted in ascending order.

Input: line 1 is nums1 as a JSON array; line 2 is nums2 as a JSON array.
Output: a JSON array of the unique common values, sorted ascending.

title: Power of Three
description:
Given an integer n, return true if it is a power of three. Otherwise, return false.

An integer n is a power of three if there exists an integer x such that n == 3^x.

Input: a single integer.
Output: 'true' or 'false'.

title: Ugly Number
description:
An ugly number is a positive integer whose prime factors are limited to 2, 3, and 5.

Given an integer n, return true if n is an ugly number.

By convention, 1 is treated as an ugly number (it has no prime factors).

Input: a single integer.
Output: 'true' or 'false'.

examples.explanation: 1 has no prime factors, so it is ugly by convention.
14 = 2 * 7, and 7 is not allowed.

title: Arranging Coins
description:
You have n coins and you want to build a staircase. The staircase consists of k rows where the i-th row has exactly i coins. The last row of the staircase may be incomplete.

Given the integer n, return the number of complete rows of the staircase you can build.

Input: a single non-negative integer.
Output: the number of complete rows.

examples.explanation: Rows of 1 and 2 coins use 3 coins; the third row would need 3 but only 2 remain.

title: Greatest Common Divisor
description:
Given two positive integers a and b, return their greatest common divisor: the largest positive integer that divides both a and b without a remainder.

Input: line 1 is a; line 2 is b.
Output: gcd(a, b).

examples.explanation: 7 and 5 are coprime.

title: First Unique Character in a String
description:
Given a string s, return the index of the first non-repeating character in it. If it does not exist, return -1.

Input: the string s (lowercase English letters).
Output: the index of the first unique character, or -1.
constraints: s consists of only lowercase English letters.

title: Running Sum of 1d Array
description:
Given an array nums, the running sum of an array is defined as runningSum[i] = sum(nums[0..i]).

Return the running sum of nums.

Input: a JSON array of integers.
Output: a JSON array of the running sums.

title: Happy Number
description:
A happy number is defined by the following process: starting with any positive integer, replace the number by the sum of the squares of its digits, and repeat until the number equals 1 (where it stays), or it loops endlessly in a cycle that never includes 1.

Return true if n is a happy number, and false otherwise.

Input: a single positive integer.
Output: 'true' or 'false'.

title: Perfect Number
description:
A perfect number is a positive integer that is equal to the sum of its positive divisors, excluding the number itself.

Given an integer n, return true if n is a perfect number, otherwise return false.

Input: a single positive integer.
Output: 'true' or 'false'.

title: Power of Four
description:
Given an integer n, return true if it is a power of four, otherwise return false.

An integer n is a power of four if there exists an integer x such that n == 4^x.

Input: a single integer.
Output: 'true' or 'false'.

title: Factorial Trailing Zeroes
description:
Given an integer n, return the number of trailing zeroes in n! (n factorial).

Note: n! = n * (n - 1) * (n - 2) * ... * 3 * 2 * 1.

Input: a single integer.
Output: the count of trailing zeroes.

examples.explanation: 3! = 6, no trailing zero.
5! = 120, one trailing zero.

title: Count Odd Numbers in an Interval Range
description:
Given two non-negative integers low and high, return the count of odd numbers between low and high (inclusive).

Input: line 1 is low; line 2 is high.
Output: the count of odd numbers.

examples.explanation: The odd numbers are 3, 5, 7.
The odd number is 9.

title: Sum of Two Integers
description:
Given two integers a and b, return the sum of the two integers without using the operators + and -.

Input: line 1 is a; line 2 is b.
Output: the sum a + b.

title: Array Partition
description:
Given an integer array nums of 2n integers, group these integers into n pairs (a1, b1), (a2, b2), ..., (an, bn) such that the sum of min(ai, bi) for all i is maximized. Return the maximized sum.

Input: an array of 2n integers.
Output: the maximized sum.

title: Maximum Product of Two Elements
description:
Given the array of integers nums, you will choose two different indices i and j of that array. Return the maximum value of (nums[i] - 1) * (nums[j] - 1).

Input: an array of integers.
Output: the maximum product.

examples.explanation: Choosing the two 5s: (5-1)*(5-1) = 16.

title: Candy
description:
There are n children standing in a line. Each child is assigned a rating value given in the integer array ratings.

You are giving candies to these children subject to the following requirements:
- Each child must have at least one candy.
- Children with a higher rating get more candies than their neighbors.

Return the minimum number of candies you need to have to distribute the candies to the children.

Input: an array of integer ratings.
Output: the minimum total number of candies.

examples.explanation: You can allocate 2, 1, 2 candies respectively.
Allocate 1, 2, 1 candies; the third child gets 1 candy, which satisfies the requirements.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock III
description:
You are given an array prices where prices[i] is the price of a given stock on the i-th day.

Find the maximum profit you can achieve. You may complete at most two transactions.

Note: You may not engage in multiple transactions simultaneously (you must sell the stock before you buy again).

Input: an array of stock prices.
Output: the maximum achievable profit.

examples.explanation: Buy on day 4 (price 0) and sell on day 6 (price 3), profit 3; then buy on day 7 (price 1) and sell on day 8 (price 4), profit 3. Total = 6.
Buy on day 1 and sell on day 5; a single transaction of profit 4 is optimal.
Prices only fall, so no transaction is made and profit is 0.

title: Maximum Gap
description:
Given an integer array nums, return the maximum difference between two successive elements in its sorted form. If the array contains less than two elements, return 0.

You must write an algorithm that runs in linear time and uses linear extra space.

Input: an array of integers.
Output: the maximum gap between successive elements once sorted.

examples.explanation: The sorted form is [1,3,6,9]; either (3,6) or (6,9) has the maximum gap of 3.
The array contains less than two elements, so return 0.

title: Count of Smaller Numbers After Self
description:
Given an integer array nums, return an integer array counts where counts[i] is the number of smaller elements to the right of nums[i].

Input: an array of integers.
Output: an array counts of the same length.

examples.explanation: To the right of 5 there are two smaller (2 and 1); right of 2 there is one (1); right of 6 there is one (1); right of 1 there are none.

title: Longest Valid Parentheses
description:
Given a string containing just the characters '(' and ')', return the length of the longest valid (well-formed) parentheses substring.

A substring is valid if every opening bracket has a matching closing bracket that appears after it, and the brackets are correctly nested.

Input: a single line containing the string (it may be empty).
Output: the length of the longest valid parentheses substring.

examples.explanation: The longest valid substring is "()", of length 2.
The longest valid substring is "()()", of length 4.
There is no valid substring in an empty string.

title: Split Array Largest Sum
description:
Given an integer array nums and an integer k, split nums into k non-empty contiguous subarrays.

Write an algorithm to minimise the largest sum among these k subarrays, and return that minimised largest sum.

Input: line 1 is an array of integers, line 2 is the integer k.
Output: the smallest possible value of the largest subarray sum.

examples.explanation: The best split is [7,2,5] and [10,8]; the largest sum is 18, and no split does better.
Split into [1,2,3] and [4,5]; the largest sum is 9.
Every element becomes its own subarray, so the largest sum is 4.

title: Number of Digit One
description:
Given an integer n, count the total number of times the digit 1 appears in all non-negative integers less than or equal to n.

A single number can contribute more than once: 11 contains the digit 1 twice, so it counts twice.

Input: a single integer n.
Output: the total number of times the digit 1 appears.

examples.explanation: The digit 1 appears in 1, 10, 11 (twice), 12 and 13, giving 6 occurrences.
Only the number 0 is in range, and it contains no digit 1.
1 appears once in each of 1 and 21..91, twice in 11, and in every number from 10 to 19 and in 100.

title: Super Egg Drop
description:
You are given k identical eggs and a building with n floors numbered from 1 to n.

There is a floor f, with 0 <= f <= n, such that an egg dropped from any floor above f breaks, and an egg dropped from floor f or below does not. Each move you take one unbroken egg and drop it from a floor of your choice; an egg that breaks cannot be reused, and one that survives can be dropped again.

Return the minimum number of moves that is always enough to determine f, no matter where f actually is.

Input: line 1 is k, the number of eggs; line 2 is n, the number of floors.
Output: the minimum number of moves needed in the worst case.

examples.explanation: With one egg you must search upward one floor at a time: drop from floor 1, and if it survives drop from floor 2.
Three moves are always enough with two eggs, and two moves are not.
Four moves suffice for 14 floors once a third egg is available.

title: Minimum Path Sum
description:
Given an m x n grid filled with non-negative numbers, find a path from the top-left cell to the bottom-right cell that minimises the sum of the numbers along the path.

You may only ever move one cell to the right or one cell down.

Input: a single line holding the grid as a list of rows, e.g. [[1,3,1],[1,5,1]].
Output: the smallest achievable path sum.

examples.explanation: The path 1 -> 3 -> 1 -> 1 -> 1 sums to 7, which is the smallest possible.
The path 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 6 sums to 12.
A single cell is both the start and the end, so the answer is that cell.

title: Number of Provinces
description:
There are n cities. Some of them are connected directly, and if city a is connected to city b and city b is connected to city c, then a and c are connected indirectly. A province is a group of cities that are all connected to each other, directly or indirectly, and which has no connection to any city outside the group.

You are given an n x n matrix isConnected where isConnected[i][j] is 1 if the i-th and j-th cities are directly connected and 0 otherwise. Return the number of provinces.

Input: a single line holding the matrix as a list of rows, e.g. [[1,1,0],[1,1,0],[0,0,1]].
Output: the number of provinces.

examples.explanation: Cities 0 and 1 form one province and city 2 forms another.
No city is connected to any other, so each is its own province.
Cities 0, 1 and 2 are linked in a chain, so they form a single province alongside the lone city 3.

title: Unique Paths III
description:
You are given an m x n grid where each cell is one of the following:

1 is the starting square (there is exactly one), 2 is the ending square (there is exactly one), 0 is an empty square you may walk over, and -1 is an obstacle you may not enter.

Return the number of distinct four-directional walks from the starting square to the ending square that step on every non-obstacle square exactly once.

Input: a single line holding the grid as a list of rows, e.g. [[1,0,0,0],[0,0,2,-1]].
Output: the number of such walks.

examples.explanation: Two walks cover all ten walkable squares before finishing on the 2.
With no obstacle there are four full-coverage walks.
Any walk from the 1 to the 2 has to skip a square, so no valid walk exists.

constraints: there is exactly one 1 and exactly one 2

title: Course Schedule
description:
There are numCourses courses labelled from 0 to numCourses - 1. You are given a list of prerequisite pairs, where the pair [a, b] means you must take course b before course a.

Return true if it is possible to finish every course, and false otherwise. It is impossible exactly when the prerequisites contain a cycle.

Input: line 1 is the integer numCourses, line 2 is the list of prerequisite pairs, e.g. [[1,0]]. An empty list is written as [].
Output: 'true' or 'false'.

examples.explanation: Take course 0 first, then course 1.
Each course requires the other, so neither can be taken first.
With no prerequisites the courses can be taken in any order.

title: Minimum Size Subarray Sum
description:
Given an array of positive integers nums and a positive integer target, return the minimal length of a contiguous subarray whose sum is greater than or equal to target.

If there is no such subarray, return 0 instead.

Input: line 1 is the array, e.g. [2,3,1,2,4,3]; line 2 is target.
Output: the minimal length, or 0.

examples.explanation: The subarray [4,3] has sum 7 and is the shortest that reaches the target.
A single 4 already reaches the target.
The whole array sums to 8, so no subarray reaches 11.

title: Longest Common Subsequence
description:
Given two strings text1 and text2, return the length of their longest common subsequence. If there is no common subsequence, return 0.

A subsequence of a string is a new string formed from the original by deleting some (possibly no) characters without changing the relative order of the remaining characters. A common subsequence is a subsequence of both strings.

Input: line 1 is text1; line 2 is text2.
Output: the length of the longest common subsequence.

examples.explanation: The longest common subsequence is "ace".
The whole string is common to both.
There is no common character.

constraints: text1 and text2 consist of lowercase English characters.

title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
description:
You are given a string s and an integer k. You may choose any character of the string and change it to any other uppercase English character, and you may do this at most k times.

Return the length of the longest substring containing the same letter you can obtain after performing those changes.

Input: line 1 is s; line 2 is k.
Output: the length of the longest achievable run.

examples.explanation: Change both A's into B's, or both B's into A's.
Change the middle A into a B to get "AABBBBA", which contains "BBBB".
With no changes allowed the best run is a single character.

constraints: s consists of only uppercase English letters.

title: Rotting Oranges
description:
You are given a grid where each cell is 0 (empty), 1 (a fresh orange) or 2 (a rotten orange).

Every minute, any fresh orange that is horizontally or vertically adjacent to a rotten orange becomes rotten. Return the minimum number of minutes until no cell has a fresh orange. If that is impossible, return -1.

Input: a single line holding the grid as a list of rows, e.g. [[2,1,1],[1,1,0],[0,1,1]].
Output: the number of minutes, or -1.

examples.explanation: The rot spreads outward from the top-left corner and reaches the last orange after 4 minutes.
The orange in the bottom-left corner is never reached.
There are no fresh oranges, so zero minutes are needed.

title: Max Area of Island
description:
You are given a binary grid where 1 marks land and 0 marks water. An island is a group of 1s connected horizontally or vertically, and the grid is surrounded by water on all four edges.

The area of an island is the number of cells with value 1 in that island. Return the maximum area of an island in the grid, or 0 if there is no island.

Input: a single line holding the grid as a list of rows, e.g. [[1,1,0],[0,1,0]].
Output: the maximum island area.

examples.explanation: All five land cells are connected into one island.
Diagonal cells are not connected, so each island has area 1.
There is no land at all.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
description:
Given an integer array nums, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

A subsequence is formed by deleting some (possibly no) elements without changing the order of the remaining elements.

Input: an array of integers.
Output: the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

examples.explanation: One longest increasing subsequence is [2,3,7,101].
One longest increasing subsequence is [0,1,2,3].
Equal values are not strictly increasing, so only one element can be used.

title: Last Stone Weight
description:
You are given an array of integers stones where stones[i] is the weight of the i-th stone.

Each turn, take the two heaviest stones x and y with x <= y and smash them together: if x == y both are destroyed, otherwise the stone of weight y - x is put back. Repeat until at most one stone is left.

Return the weight of the last remaining stone, or 0 if none remains.

Input: an array of positive integers.
Output: the weight of the last stone, or 0.

examples.explanation: Smash 8 and 7 to get 1, then 4 and 2 to get 2, then 2 and 1 to get 1, then 1 and 1 destroy each other, leaving 1.
The two equal stones destroy each other.
A single stone is never smashed.

title: Distinct Subsequences
description:
Given two strings s and t, return the number of distinct subsequences of s which equal t.

A subsequence is formed by deleting some (possibly no) characters of s without changing the order of the remaining characters. Two subsequences are distinct when they use different sets of positions, even if they read the same.

Input: line 1 is s; line 2 is t.
Output: the number of distinct subsequences.

examples.explanation: There are three ways to choose which of the three b's to drop.
Five different position sets in "babgbag" spell "bag".
No subsequence of s equals t.

constraints: s and t consist of English letters.
The answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer.

title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
description:
Given an integer matrix, return the length of the longest strictly increasing path.

From each cell you may move up, down, left or right, and only onto a strictly larger value. You may not move diagonally or step outside the matrix.

Input: a single line holding the matrix as a list of rows, e.g. [[9,9,4],[6,6,8],[2,1,1]].
Output: the number of cells on the longest increasing path.

examples.explanation: The longest increasing path is 1 -> 2 -> 6 -> 9.
The longest increasing path is 3 -> 4 -> 5 -> 6.
A single cell is a path of length 1.

title: Network Delay Time
description:
You are given a network of n nodes labelled from 1 to n, and a list of travel times as directed edges times[i] = [ui, vi, wi], where ui is the source node, vi is the target node and wi is the time a signal takes to travel from source to target.

A signal is sent from node k. Return the time it takes for all n nodes to receive the signal, which is the longest of the shortest arrival times. If it is impossible for every node to receive the signal, return -1.

Input: line 1 is the list of edges, e.g. [[2,1,1],[2,3,1],[3,4,1]]. An empty list is written as []. Line 2 is the integer n, line 3 is the integer k.
Output: the time for every node to receive the signal, or -1.

examples.explanation: Nodes 1 and 3 receive the signal after 1, and node 4 receives it after 2, so the last arrival is at time 2.
The signal travels the single edge from node 1 to node 2 in time 1.
The edge only points from 1 to 2, so a signal starting at node 2 never reaches node 1.

title: Is Graph Bipartite?
description:
There is an undirected graph with n nodes labelled from 0 to n - 1. You are given the graph as an adjacency list, where graph[u] is the list of nodes adjacent to node u.

The graph is bipartite if its nodes can be split into two sets A and B such that every edge joins one node in A to one node in B. Return true if the graph is bipartite, and false otherwise. The graph may be disconnected.

Input: a single line holding the adjacency list, e.g. [[1,3],[0,2],[1,3],[0,2]]. A node with no neighbours is written as [].
Output: 'true' or 'false'.

examples.explanation: Nodes 0, 1 and 2 form a triangle, an odd cycle, so no two-way split can separate every edge.
Split the nodes into {0, 2} and {1, 3}; every edge joins the two sets.
A single node with no edges is trivially bipartite.

constraints: all values of graph[u] are distinct
if graph[u] contains v, then graph[v] contains u

title: Letter Combinations of a Phone Number
description:
Given a string containing digits from 2-9 inclusive, return every letter combination the number could spell on a telephone keypad.

The mapping is the one printed on the keys: 2 -> abc, 3 -> def, 4 -> ghi, 5 -> jkl, 6 -> mno, 7 -> pqrs, 8 -> tuv, 9 -> wxyz. The digit 1 carries no letters and never appears in the input.

Each combination must spell its letters in the SAME ORDER as the digits that produced them: the first letter comes from the first digit, the second from the second, and so on. The combinations themselves may be returned in ANY ORDER - this problem is judged as a set, so your answer is accepted however you order the list.

Input: a single line holding the digit string. An empty input is an empty line.
Output: a compact JSON array of strings, e.g. ["ad","ae","af"]. Return [] when the input is empty.

examples.explanation: 2 contributes one of a, b, c and 3 contributes one of d, e, f, so there are 3 x 3 = 9 combinations. Any ordering of the nine is accepted.
With no digits there is nothing to spell, so the answer is the empty list - not a list holding the empty string.
A single digit yields one combination per letter on that key.

constraints: digits[i] is a digit in the range ['2', '9']
